title: Sum and collect for your types
description:
Make two types fit into iterator chains:

- `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)] struct Meters(f64)` with `impl Sum` (for `Meters` items) and `impl<'a> Sum<&'a Meters>` (for references), so both `v.into_iter().sum::<Meters>()` and `v.iter().sum::<Meters>()` work.
- `#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)] struct Stats { count: usize, mean: f64, max: f64 }` with `impl FromIterator<f64>`, so `[1.0, 2.0].into_iter().collect::<Stats>()` works. No items gives `count 0`, `mean 0.0` and `max` of `f64::NEG_INFINITY`.
hints: `impl Sum for Meters { fn sum<I: Iterator<Item = Meters>>(iter: I) -> Meters { ... } }`; the reference version is the same with `Item = &'a Meters` (lesson 8.04).
`FromIterator::from_iter` receives anything `IntoIterator`; loop over it once, keeping the count, the total and the maximum.
